venture.description: Eco-friendly, dehydrated laundry detergent sheets and other cleaning products packaged without plastic.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders present their eco-friendly, plastic-free laundry detergent sheets and ask for 500k for 5 percent.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: The founders demonstrate how the laundry sheet dissolves completely in a bottle of cold water when shaken.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel asks what the primary ingredients of the laundry sheets are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris explains the primary ingredients are derived from coconut oil and are plant-based, without synthetic chemicals.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks about the founders' backgrounds and their specific roles in the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris shares his story as a former military helicopter pilot whose lungs were damaged by burning trash in Iraq.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: The other Chris explains he met his co-founder in 2018 and wanted to start a business with a purpose.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks what specific products are included in their line and what they sell.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris explains they have 46 different SKUs, including floor cleaners and scent boosters, all focused on reducing plastic.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks when the company officially launched its products to the public.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris states they officially launched to the public in January 2020.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel asks what their total sales revenue was for the year 2020.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris reports they achieved just over 2 million dollars in total sales in 2020.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel asks what percentage of their sales comes from their number one selling item.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Chris clarifies that their laundry sheets are their top-selling product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel asks for the specific sales figure for the laundry sheets out of the 2 million total.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris says they sold 1.2 million in sheets and mentions an exclusivity agreement with Kimberly Clark.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they have to pay a royalty to Kimberly Clark for the patent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris confirms that they do pay a royalty.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks to clarify if they are the only ones allowed to use the patent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris confirms the patent is exclusive to them as long as they pay their annual royalties.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin challenges that they do not own the patent and asks how long the agreement lasts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris states the agreement lasts until October 2024.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks what happens after 2024 and if they have an option to renew the agreement.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris admits that the agreement simply expires.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara exits, citing concerns over the expiring patent, too many SKUs, and their lack of salesmanship.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris counters Barbara's claim by stating they are on track to do 7 million in sales this year.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks to verify if they are really growing from 2 million to 7 million in one year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris confirms that the projection is correct.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how they achieved such high sales growth despite Barbara's critique of their sales skills.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris explains they built their sales through aggressive advertising campaigns and user-generated content.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks if they used quick videos for their advertising.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris confirms they used quick videos featuring customer testimonials.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks which platforms they used to run their video advertisements.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Chris lists social platforms like Pinterest and AdWords, noting his background in e-commerce marketing.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin exits because he is already invested in a competing company called Blueland.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori exits, stating she likes the mission but the valuation does not excite her.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks what they plan to do with the 500k investment and why they need a shark.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris explains they want to use the funds to expand their business globally.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark exits, feeling that global expansion is too expensive and risky for his investment strategy.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel asks how confident they are in hitting their 7 million sales projection for the year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris cites their 21,000 monthly subscribers and an upcoming retail launch in Target as reasons for confidence.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel offers 500k for 10 percent of the company, impressed by their traction and mission.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris counters Daniel's offer, asking if he would accept 500k for 8 percent equity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel revises his offer to 500k for 8 percent equity plus 2 percent in advisory shares.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris asks to clarify if the revised offer effectively means 500k for 10 percent total.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel confirms that the total equity and advisory shares equal 10 percent.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Chris asks for a brief moment to discuss the offer privately with his co-founder.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chris accepts Daniel's revised offer of 500k for 8 percent equity and 2 percent advisory shares.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders and Daniel celebrate the deal with cheers and thanks.
